model: Symbio 800 (SCC IntelliPak) / Symbio 700 - touch-screen zone sensor points
equipment_type: Rooftop unit controller (zone sensor interaction subset)
applies_to: Trane single-zone equipment on Symbio 700 and IntelliPak units on Symbio 800 (SCC), used with the commercial touch-screen programmable zone sensor.
summary: This short list shows which Symbio 700 / Symbio 800 (SCC IntelliPak) objects the Trane commercial touch-screen programmable zone sensor reads and writes. It covers space temperature, setpoints and offsets, heat/cool mode request and status, occupancy request, fan mode and economizer enable setpoints. The sensor and controller talk BACnet MS/TP.
notes: This is a SUBSET: only the Symbio objects the touch-screen zone sensor uses (Table 6 of BAS-SVP080A, p18), not the controller's full points list. The table's System Control Command row is N/A for Symbio and is left out.
Access is inferred: the doc has no read/write column. Request, setpoint and command objects the sensor writes are shown as W; inputs as R.

Symbio uses last-in arbitration, so the sensor does not manage Out_Of_Service on these objects (unlike UC400 and ReliaTel). AV 10150/AV 10170 can be switched In Use / Not Used from the sensor setup menu.
Matching sensor objects (AV 100, AV 44, AV 43, MV 140, MV 16, MV 112, MI 33, MV 17, AV 260, AV 261) belong to the sensor itself. Symbio 700 multiple-zone systems are not supported.
The guide's table prints Space Temperature BAS as 'AV1014'; that is a typo for AV 10114, the object number in Trane's full Symbio 700 points lists.

The names are the sensor guide's labels. On Symbio 700 the controller itself names these AI 10218 Space Temperature Input, MV 10104 Heat Cool Mode Request, MI 10101 Heat Cool Mode Status, AV 10150 Economizer Outdoor Air Enable Setpoint BAS and AV 10170 Economizer Outdoor Air Enthalpy Enable Setpoint BAS. AI 10173 Supply Fan Speed Status is in the Symbio 800 IntelliPak list but not in the Symbio 700 lists. MV 10106 on Symbio 700 also has 5 = Auto.

integration.summary: Use the BMS mainly for monitoring and alarms when the touch-screen sensor runs the unit. The sensor writes occupancy, mode, fan and setpoints; read mode status and fan speed. Because Symbio arbitrates last-in, any BMS write to the same objects simply overrides the sensor until it writes again.

minimum_points.name: Supply Fan Configuration Command
minimum_points.why: Fan mode: Inactive = Auto, Active = On

minimum_points.name: Space Temperature BAS
minimum_points.why: Space temperature in use by the unit

integration.enable: The touch-screen sensor writes the occupancy, mode, fan and setpoint objects; Symbio uses last-in arbitration so no Out_Of_Service handling is needed. The guide recommends leaving control with the sensor.
integration.remote_sensors: Space Temperature BAS normally comes from the sensor. Space Temperature Local is the unit's hard-wired sensor.
setup: The sensor talks BACnet MS/TP only; default baud 76800 (leave the default).
Sensor and unit controller should share an MS/TP link where possible to reduce communication loss.
Trane best practice device ID: MS/TP network number followed by the MAC address (e.g. network 11, MAC 001 = 11001).
gotchas: With last-in arbitration a BMS write and the sensor overwrite each other; pick one owner for each command point.

The sensor guide calls Symbio arbitration 'last-in', but Trane's Symbio 700 integration guide (BAS-SVP085B) treats AV 10127 as a commandable object: a wired setpoint sits at priority 15 and Air-Fi at 14, so a BMS writing above 14 wins. Read the priority array before assuming who owns the setpoint.

source.title: Touch Screen Programmable Zone Sensor Integration Guide (Tracer UC400-B, Symbio 400-B/500/700/800, ReliaTel)
